name: Standing I-Y-T Raise
summary: A bodyweight shoulder and postural mobility exercise combining overhead, diagonal, and lateral arm raises.

setup: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and knees soft.
Brace your core, draw your ribs down, and let your arms hang naturally at your sides with thumbs pointing forward.
steps: Raise both arms directly forward and overhead into an 'I' position until fully elevated, then lower with control to your sides.
Raise both arms at roughly a 45-degree angle from your torso into a 'Y' position with thumbs pointing up and back, then lower smoothly.
Raise both arms directly out to the sides into a 'T' position until parallel with the floor, squeezing your shoulder blades together, then return to the starting position.
instructions.breathing: Inhale as you raise your arms in each direction to support thoracic extension, and exhale as you lower them.
cues: Keep shoulders down away from your ears.
Do not arch your lower back.

common_faults.fault: Hyperextending the lumbar spine to gain overhead range of motion.
common_faults.correction: Keep your abdominals braced and ribcage pulled down throughout all three positions.

common_faults.fault: Shrugging the upper traps excessively during the raises.
common_faults.correction: Focus on depressing your scapulae and lifting via mid and lower trap activation rather than shrugging.

precautions: Move through a pain-free range of motion if you experience shoulder impingement.
